_comment: Labels for issue priority triage (ADR-0005). The apply job creates any that are missing; it never edits or deletes an existing label. Severity, reach, priority and needs-triage are the same in every project. The area labels are this project's own: replace the examples with the project's parts (one per top-level component or source folder is a good start), keep each description under 100 characters, and list the same areas in prompt.md. Owners map an area to the GitHub login assigned when an issue has no assignee; "*" is the fallback.

sev:critical.description: Silently wrong figure, lost or doubled activity, unauthenticated access, a secret leaks

sev:major.description: Code run via crafted input, data leak, safety check bypassed, crash, core feature broken

sev:minor.description: Wrong behaviour with a workaround, or a visible degradation

sev:trivial.description: Cosmetic, wording, docs, or a test-only gap

reach:edge.description: Needs an unusual setup, input or timing

reach:adversarial.description: Only triggers when someone sets it up on purpose

area:engine.description: Calculation engine: lots, valuation, TTWROR, IZF, matching, taxes

area:import.description: ofxstatement plugins, OFX, Parqet CSV and manual entry (adapters)

area:market-data.description: Price, split and FX providers: yfinance, ECB, manual CSV, later IBKR

area:cli.description: The depot command, its report views and the HTML report

area:api.description: Django Ninja API, login and settings (web)

area:ci.description: Workflows, the nox gate, build and release tooling

area:docs.description: ADRs, proposals, architecture, the threat model and other docs

priority:P0.description: Drop other work, fix now, block the release (ADR-0005)

priority:P2.description: Next milestone, or whenever it fits (ADR-0005)

needs-triage.description: Severity or reach could not be placed; says what is missing
